findings.requirement_type: Named Insured — Inc vs LLC Entity-Type Mismatch (Hanover Auto)
findings.contract_quote: Run-Test confirmed legal entity = 'Runbeck Election Services, LLC' (per Hartford ML, Arch Security, Convex Excess, AmTrust Cyber Dec pages and AmTrust Policy Change #1 dated 4/1/2025 which expressly corrected the Cyber Named Insured to LLC).
findings.contract_page: Cross-program — confirmed by AmTrust Cyber Policy Change #1, page 2
findings.policy_quote: First Named Insured: 'Runbeck Election Services Inc'
findings.gap_description: The Hanover Commercial Auto Dec lists 'Runbeck Election Services Inc' as First Named Insured. The client's true legal entity is an LLC, as confirmed by four other in-force policies (Hartford ML, Arch Security CGL, Convex Excess Tech E&O, AmTrust Cyber — the latter expressly corrected via Policy Change #1 effective 4/1/2025). The Inc-vs-LLC asymmetry persists across five program policies (WC, Auto, Commercial Package, Umbrella, Gemini E&O) while four name the LLC correctly. Two distinct legal persons are named on the program for the same operating company. Form-of-Business field on the Auto Dec almost certainly reads 'Corporation,' compounding the documentary mismatch. In a contested claim, plaintiff counsel will argue the policyholder of record (Inc) is not the entity that incurred the loss (LLC), creating standing/insurable-interest litigation that delays defense and forces a coverage-by-litigation outcome.
findings.plain_english: Five of your nine policies — including the Auto policy — name 'Runbeck Election Services Inc.' But your real company is 'Runbeck Election Services, LLC.' Inc and LLC are two different legal entities. Your Cyber carrier already fixed this for the Cyber policy back on 4/1/2025; nobody propagated that fix to the rest of the program. If a serious auto claim hits, the carrier or a plaintiff can argue that the entity on the policy isn't the entity that operated the truck — which buys you weeks of fighting before defense even starts.
findings.recommendation: Immediately request Policy Change endorsements (IL 12 01 or carrier equivalent) on Hanover Auto, Hanover Commercial Package, Hanover Umbrella, Gemini Professional Liability, and Hanover WC to correct First Named Insured to 'Runbeck Election Services, LLC' and Form of Business to 'Limited Liability Company.' Use the AmTrust Cyber Policy Change #1 as a template. Get all five corrections back-dated to 4/1/2025 inception so there is no gap.
discoveryQuestions: When did Runbeck convert from Inc to LLC, and was the broker notified at that time to update every policy in the program?
Has anyone ever submitted a claim where the carrier asked you to prove the entity on the Dec page is the same entity that suffered the loss?
Your AmTrust Cyber carrier corrected the entity name in Policy Change #1 effective 4/1/2025 — do you know why that correction wasn't applied to the other eight policies at the same renewal?
If a plaintiff sued 'Runbeck Election Services, LLC' for an auto accident, how comfortable would you be relying on a policy issued to 'Runbeck Election Services Inc' to fund your defense?

findings.requirement_type: Designated Entity Cancellation Notice — Maricopa County Missing from Hanover Auto
findings.contract_quote: Maricopa contract §8.2.15 (p 7) requires Maricopa County to receive 30-day designated-entity cancellation notice on all required insurance lines.
findings.policy_quote: Hanover Auto Endorsement 401-1235 12 14 (Notice of Cancellation to Designated Entity(s)) lists 8 designated entities (BLANKET WHERE REQUIRED BY WRITTEN CONTRACT, City of Boulder, Coconino County, Amazon.com Services, El Paso County, San Luis Obispo County, State of Colorado, NY State OGS) but does NOT list Maricopa County.
findings.gap_description: The Hanover Auto policy carries a Designated Entity NOC endorsement listing 8 entities, but Maricopa County — the contract counterparty for §8.2.15 — is conspicuously absent from the list. The 'BLANKET WHERE REQUIRED BY WRITTEN CONTRACT' line item provides arguable cover, but most carriers and counties require the entity to be expressly named to give effect to the contractual notice obligation. The absence is particularly visible because seven specific entities ARE named on this policy, suggesting the broker built the schedule manually and missed Maricopa.
findings.plain_english: Your Maricopa County contract requires Maricopa to get 30 days' notice if your Auto policy gets cancelled. The Auto policy DOES have a designated-entity notice endorsement — and it lists eight entities. Maricopa is not one of them. If the policy ever cancels, Maricopa won't get direct notice and you're in breach of contract.
findings.recommendation: Endorse 'Maricopa County' onto Hanover Auto Form 401-1235 with 30-day notice. Verify against the Maricopa contract address. Audit all program policies and add Maricopa to every required policy line in parallel (see related findings on each policy).
discoveryQuestions: How was the designated-entity schedule on the Auto policy built — did the broker get a list from you or pull it from prior years?
Has Maricopa ever audited your COI or NOC endorsements directly?
If the Auto policy got cancelled tomorrow, do you understand that 7 of your customer counties would get notice but Maricopa would not?

findings.requirement_type: Designated Entity Cancellation Notice — Maricopa County Missing from Arch Security Guards CGL
findings.contract_quote: Maricopa contract §8.2.15 (p 7) requires Maricopa County to receive 30-day designated-entity cancellation notice on all required insurance lines.
findings.policy_quote: Arch Security Guards CGL — no Designated Entity NOC endorsement appears in the policy.
findings.gap_description: The Arch Security Guards CGL stand-alone policy has no Designated Entity NOC endorsement. If Maricopa contract requires GL coverage with cancellation notice, and this CGL is one of the GL policies in the program (per the program summary listing both the Hanover Package GL and this Arch CGL), Maricopa is owed notice on this layer too.
findings.plain_english: Your secondary GL policy (the Security Guards-specific one with Arch) has no cancellation-notice endorsement at all. Maricopa would not be notified if it were cancelled.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with Run-Test whether the Arch Security Guards CGL is responsive to county contracts. If yes, endorse Maricopa (and other county counterparties) as designated entities with 30-day notice. If the policy is for a non-county-facing risk only, document the limited use in the broker file.
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Hanover Commercial Package Form 401-1235 (also missing Maricopa per separate finding)
discoveryQuestions: What operations does the Arch Security Guards CGL cover that the Hanover Commercial Package doesn't?
Are county contracts ever serviced by security-guard work, and would cancellation of this policy affect any county contract?

findings.requirement_type: Designated Entity Cancellation Notice — Maricopa County Missing from Hartford Management Liability
findings.contract_quote: Maricopa contract §8.2.15 (p 7) requires Maricopa County to receive 30-day designated-entity cancellation notice on all required insurance lines.
findings.policy_quote: Hartford Management Liability — no Designated Entity NOC endorsement appears in the policy.
findings.gap_description: Hartford ML carries no Designated Entity NOC endorsement. Most county contracts focus the NOC requirement on lines explicitly required by the contract (GL, Auto, WC, Cyber, E&O); Maricopa §8.2.15's 'all required' reading may or may not extend to ML. Conservative reading favors adding Maricopa to the schedule.
findings.plain_english: Maricopa contract says all required insurance lines need notice. Your D&O policy isn't a typical 'required line' for county contracts, so this is debatable — but if your contract references it, the safe play is to add Maricopa to the schedule.
findings.recommendation: Verify with Maricopa whether ML is treated as a required insurance line under §8.2. If yes, request Hartford add the Maricopa NOC endorsement. If not, document the determination.
discoveryQuestions: Does Maricopa specifically request a COI for D&O coverage at contract renewal, or only for GL/Auto/WC/Cyber/E&O?

findings.requirement_type: Designated Entity Cancellation Notice — Maricopa County Missing from Gemini Professional Liability
findings.contract_quote: Maricopa contract §8.2.15 (p 7) requires Maricopa County to receive 30-day designated-entity cancellation notice on all required insurance lines. Maricopa expressly requires Tech E&O / Professional Liability under §8.2 (per existing audit context).
findings.policy_quote: Gemini Professional Liability — no Designated Entity NOC endorsement appears in the policy.
findings.gap_description: Gemini Professional Liability — the lead E&O coverage for ballot-printing and election-mail processing claims — has no Designated Entity NOC endorsement at all. For a county contract that pays you on professional-services delivery, this is the most contractually exposed NOC gap.
findings.plain_english: Your E&O — the policy most likely to respond to a real county claim about ballot accuracy — has zero cancellation-notice protection for Maricopa or any other county. If the policy is cancelled, none of your customers know. That's a contract breach across multiple counties.
findings.recommendation: Request Gemini add a Designated Entity NOC endorsement listing Maricopa County and every other county counterparty (Sacramento, Los Angeles, Douglas CO, Coconino, El Paso, San Luis Obispo, Benton WA) with 30-day notice. Confirm Convex Excess Tech E&O follows form on this endorsement.
discoveryQuestions: When you submitted COIs to Maricopa for the current contract, did the certificate hold or did Maricopa kick it back for missing endorsements?
Has any county ever asked specifically whether they would receive direct notice if your E&O is cancelled?

findings.requirement_type: Designated Entity Cancellation Notice — Maricopa County Missing from Convex Excess Tech E&O
findings.contract_quote: Maricopa contract §8.2.15 (p 7) requires Maricopa County to receive 30-day designated-entity cancellation notice on all required insurance lines.
findings.policy_quote: Convex Excess Tech E&O — no Designated Entity NOC endorsement appears in the policy.
findings.gap_description: The $5M Convex Excess Tech E&O has no NOC endorsement. While the contract may permit follow-form on the underlying Gemini schedule, the existing audit's 'Conditional Follow-Form More Restrictive' clause finding (already on the list) makes follow-form less reliable. Direct scheduling on Convex eliminates the ambiguity.
findings.plain_english: Your Tech E&O excess has no cancellation-notice endorsement, and Convex's follow-form has carve-outs that may not extend to this kind of endorsement. Direct scheduling is the safe move.
findings.recommendation: Endorse Maricopa County and other county counterparties onto the Convex Excess Tech E&O with 30-day notice.
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Gemini Primary E&O — also missing per separate finding
discoveryQuestions: Has Convex confirmed in writing that follow-form attaches to a Designated Entity NOC endorsement issued by Gemini at primary level?

findings.requirement_type: Cross-Cutting — Sacramento, Los Angeles, Douglas (CO), San Luis Obispo, Benton (WA) Counties Not Listed as Designated Entities Anywhere in Program
findings.contract_quote: Sacramento County: 'CONTRACTOR shall provide the COUNTY with at least thirty (30) calendar days written notice of any cancellation, non-renewal, or material change in coverage.' (Sacramento Appendix G §VI). Los Angeles County contract Amendment Number Four — see contract notice provisions. Douglas County and San Luis Obispo similar standard county templates.
findings.contract_page: Sacramento Appendix G §VI; LA Amendment 4; Douglas/SLO standard
findings.policy_quote: Cross-policy NOC schedule audit: Sacramento County, Los Angeles County, Douglas County (CO), San Luis Obispo County, Benton County (WA) appear on NO Designated Entity NOC endorsement on ANY policy in the program — the only policy that lists San Luis Obispo and Douglas-related entities is Hanover Auto (and only via the partial Auto schedule).
findings.gap_description: The NOC matrix shows Sacramento, LA, Douglas (CO), and Benton (WA) — all confirmed county counterparties per the contracts in the audit set — appear on no NOC endorsement anywhere in the program. San Luis Obispo and Douglas-via-Colorado appear only on Hanover Auto pages 45–46 but not on the GL Package or Umbrella. This is a multi-county notice deficiency that runs across multiple required coverage lines.
findings.plain_english: The NOC schedules across your program look like a partial draft — they cover Coconino, El Paso, Amazon, Boulder, NY State, and a few others, but they MISS Sacramento, LA County, and Douglas Colorado, all of which are active customer contracts in the audit. If any of your policies cancels, those four counties would learn about it from a third party rather than from your broker.
findings.recommendation: Cross-policy reconciliation project: build a master list of every customer contract requiring designated-entity notice, and reconcile against every policy NOC endorsement. Add Sacramento County, Los Angeles County, Douglas County (CO), and Benton County (WA) to all required-line NOC endorsements with the longest contract-required notice period (typically 30 days, but Sacramento and LA may require longer — verify).
discoveryQuestions: How many active county contracts does Run-Test have right now, and is there a single source-of-truth list the broker reconciles to at renewal?
Has Run-Test ever had a county contract terminated for cause due to insurance non-compliance — and if so, what triggered it?
If a policy non-renewed mid-county-contract, does Run-Test have an internal process to notify counties directly even if the broker doesn't?
Does the legal team review COI/NOC schedules at contract execution, or rely on the broker to validate compliance?
